ordered_diagnoses: Autoimmune encephalitis with NMDA receptor antibodies

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of altered mental status with myoclonus
key_facts: History of insomnia and irritable bowel syndrome
Taking vitamin D3, vitamin K, manganese, and activated charcoal
Normal coordination, sensation, and cranial nerves
Normal laboratory tests including CBC, renal, hepatic, and thyroid function
Lumbar puncture showed protein 47 mg/dL and 10 WBC/μL
Brain MRI on hospital day 5 was normal

shortlist.label: Autoimmune encephalitis with NMDA receptor antibodies
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of altered mental status and myoclonus, with empiric treatment and lack of improvement on antivirals and antibiotics

shortlist.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of neurological symptoms and myoclonus, despite normal initial laboratory tests and imaging

shortlist.label: Hashimoto encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Altered mental status and myoclonus, with potential autoimmune etiology

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Initial empiric treatment with acyclovir, despite lack of clear improvement

shortlist.label: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of altered mental status and myoclonus, with potential for rare but serious infectious etiology

raw.rationale: The patient's rapid progression of symptoms, including myoclonus, confusion, and somnolence, despite normal laboratory tests and lack of response to antivirals and antibiotics, is consistent with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, a rare and degenerative neurological disorder

rejected.label: Autoimmune encephalitis with NMDA receptor antibodies
rejected.why: Lack of response to intravenous immunoglobulin and normal laboratory tests make this less likely

rejected.label: Hashimoto encephalopathy
rejected.why: Normal thyroid function tests and lack of response to treatment for autoimmune encephalitis make this less likely

rejected.label: Herpes simplex encephalitis
rejected.why: Normal noncontrast brain CT and lack of response to antivirals make this less likely

rejected.label: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis
rejected.why: Lack of history of measles infection and normal laboratory tests make this less likely
